text:
maria: Kicking off the pricing/packaging/usage Q&A thread from today's all-hands. Drop short questions about rate limits, quotas, credits, or packaging here — Jamal and Eva are on for answers. Notes: https://redwood.example.com/all-hands/pricing-qa :spiral_notepad:
jamal: Thanks! I'll answer product-side specifics. If we need legal/finance details Diego and Priya will chime in.
jamal: Quick summary up front: hosted API defaults are conservative (free tier), paid accounts can request increases or switch to Dedicated for guaranteed throughput.
alex: Are hosted API rate limits enforced per API key or per account? And what about burst behavior?
jamal: Good Q. Default enforcement is per-API-key, with a soft per-account safety throttle to prevent abuse. Free tier = 60 req/min by default; paid starter = 600 req/min. Bursts allowed up to ~2x sustained for a short window. We surface `X-RateLimit-*` headers.
priya: How do we communicate per-minute vs per-second limits to customers? Customers often ask for per-second numbers.
jamal: We publish both in the docs. Typical mapping: 600 req/min -> 10 req/sec sustained, bursts to 20 req/sec. Also show examples for tokens/sec for generation-heavy workloads.
alex: For burst handling, do we 429 or queue?
jamal: Hosted: 429 for throttled requests. For Dedicated you can configure queueing/slowdown policies in the Console (Admin > Capacity > Overload policy). We also have an auto-fallback option to compatible, cheaper model variants if you opt in.
diego: On credits: free credits issued at sign-up expire after 90 days. Promotional enterprise credits are negotiable and *may* have custom expiry in contract. Credits always apply to usage, not reserved capacity.
maria: Clarify: reserved/dedicated capacity billing is a commit, not consumed from credits, right?
diego: Correct — Dedicated is a monthly/annual committed SKU. Credits reduce hosted-API usage charges only, not reserved capacity fees.
priya: What happens if a team hits a quota mid-promo? Do we auto-bump them?
priya: (asking from support perspective)
jamal: We don't auto-upgrade accounts. Support can help fast-track a quota increase for paid customers. For free tier we direct teams to upgrade or request an exception with justification.
alex: Any changes planned to the free-tier limits this quarter?
jamal: No immediate changes. We're exploring a small increase for educational non-profits, but nothing global yet.
eva: High-level: transparency is our priority — clearer docs and predictable SLOs. We're investing in console UX so teams can see current throttle buckets and projected spend by route.
priya: Billing question: if a paid account uses promo credits, do they still appear on invoices?
diego: Yes — invoices show gross usage, discounts/credits, and net due. Promo credits reduce net charges but still appear line-itemed for audit.
alex: Are rate limits different for embeddings vs chat/generation?
jamal: Yes — embeddings are measured in embedding units (calls per minute) and also token-equivalent for billing. Generation/chat is token-based for billing and request rate-limited by calls/min and tokens/sec guidance. Docs have an embeddings-specific section with examples.
priya: Any recommended headers/examples we should tell customers to monitor?
jamal: We recommend looking at: `X-RateLimit-Limit`, `X-RateLimit-Remaining`, `X-RateLimit-Reset` and our `X-Request-Id` for support. Example curl snippet to surface them:

```
curl -i \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" \
  https://api.redwood.example.com/v1/generate?model=redwood-1
```

jamal: The `-i` shows the headers. Add logging around those headers for production.
maria: Security/abuse question: how do we detect noisy neighbors or abusive keys?
jamal: We have automated heuristics + manual support review. Abuse triggers can lead to temporary key pause and an email to the admin. For enterprise we offer stricter per-route whitelisting and IP allowlists.
eva: We also want to offer a clearer self-serve path for quota appeals in the Console by EOY.
priya: For internal follow-up: should support open tickets for every quota bump request?
priya: (to ensure we capture context)
diego: Yes please — include usage samples, `X-Request-Id`s and a short justification. That speeds approvals.
redwood-docs-bot: Updated pricing/limits doc: https://redwood.example.com/docs/pricing#rate-limits — includes table + per-tier examples (auto-posted from notes).
maria: Thanks all — if anything unresolved tag @jamal or @priya and we'll follow up in the thread. Closing in 5. :thumbsup:
